nodes.name: Gateway Call
nodes.notes:
args_json and kwargs_json are STRINGS, not objects. n8n sub-workflow inputs
flatten nested objects unpredictably, and an Odoo domain is a nested array
(e.g. [["|",["email_norm","=",..],["phone","=",..]]]). Passing it as text and
parsing it here is the only shape that survives the boundary intact.

nodes.name: Read Odoo Config
nodes.notes:
Tables are addressed BY NAME, never by id. Ids are minted per instance, so a
name reference is the difference between this importing cleanly on a
reviewer's n8n and importing as a red node.

nodes.name: Authenticate

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", method: "call", params: { service: "common", method: "authenticate", args: [$json.odoo_db, $json.odoo_user, $json.odoo_password, {}] }, id: 1 }) }}

nodes.notes:
neverError + fullResponse, deliberately. This endpoint returns HTTP 200 for a
failed login, so the status code carries no information and the body has to
be read either way. Letting n8n decide success from the status would mark a
rejected login as a good response.

The gateway authenticates on every invocation. That is one extra round trip,
and it buys statelessness: there is no cached uid to go stale, and no
session-expiry branch to write, test and explain.

nodes.name: Odoo Call

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", method: "call", params: { service: "object", method: "execute_kw", args: [$json.odoo_db, $json.uid, $json.odoo_password, $json.model, $json.method, $json.args, $json.kwargs] }, id: 2 }) }}

nodes.notes:
No retryOnFail here on purpose. n8n's built-in retry has a fixed delay, no
jitter, and no way to distinguish 429 from 400 - and it cannot see a failure
that arrived as HTTP 200 anyway. Retry is done explicitly by the loop below,
which classifies first and backs off with jitter.

nodes.name: Retry?
nodes.notes:
True branch = another attempt is allowed. The loop is bounded twice over: by
C.RETRY.MAX_TRIES in Inspect Response, and by this node only ever seeing an
incremented attempt counter. There is no path that loops forever.

nodes.name: Backoff
nodes.notes:
Capped at 8 seconds, not 60. The gateway runs as a sub-workflow the caller
waits on, so a long sleep here holds the parent open and can blow a webhook
response window. Three tries at 0.5s, 1s, 2s costs under 4 seconds total.

nodes.name: Return
nodes.notes:
Returns ok:false rather than throwing. A gateway that throws forces every one
of its eleven callers to wrap it in error handling; a gateway that returns a
verdict lets each caller decide whether this particular failure is fatal.

parameters.content:
## LP-90 Odoo Gateway

Every Odoo read and write in the system passes through this workflow.

**The trap it exists for:** `/jsonrpc` returns **HTTP 200 when the call failed** and puts the error in the body. `Inspect Response` is the only node that knows this. Without it, a rejected write is recorded as a successful one.

**Config** lives in the `lp_config` data table, written by `LP-00 Setup and Seed`. Re-running setup re-points the whole system at a new Odoo with no node edits.

**Retry** is explicit, not `retryOnFail`: classify first (429/5xx transient, 4xx permanent), then back off with jitter, capped at 8s, max 3 tries.
